cascade.

fix: stabilize pane lifecycle and split-tree identity after portal removal

Guards and identity hints that surfaced while testing the model-owned-NSView
refactor. Without these, reshaping the split tree reused the wrong NSViewRepresentable
slot (swapping live surfaces between panes) and closing a pane null-derefed
ghostty_surface_set_focus inside first-responder swap, silently killing the process.

- Stable .id() on each recursive SplitTreeView child and on the root so SwiftUI
  rebuilds cleanly when the tree reshapes after a close
- nil-guard ghostty_surface_set_focus in become/resignFirstResponder so a
  destroyed-surface view doesn't null-deref during the responder swap
- isDestroyed flag so createSurface can't resurrect a retired view from stray
  updateNSView or viewDidMoveToWindow calls during teardown
- Defer NSView dealloc one runloop tick after destroySurface so in-flight
  ghostty callbacks (which hold unretained pointers) can drain safely

Validate activeTabID in Workspace.init against tabs list

A stale activeTabID from a corrupt persistence snapshot could leave the
workspace pointing at a tab that doesn't exist. Fall back to the first
tab instead so the UI always has a valid selection.

Add model-layer test suite and wire into check pipeline + CI

Covers SplitNode tree/resize/geometry/rebalance, TerminalTab,
Workspace, RecencyStack, AppState, WorkspaceSerializer round-trip,
Palette engine, Hotkeys, and Pane — 150 tests total. AppState gains
WorkspaceStore dependency injection so tests can run against a
tempdir. `swift test` now runs as part of `mise run check` /
`check:fix` and therefore on every CI push.

Document test workflow for contributors

Adds a `mise run test` hint and a short Contributing note pointing at
the format/lint/test pipeline so new contributors know what CI
enforces.

Split CI checks into individual steps

Each check (format, lint, test) now runs as its own step in the
Checks workflow so failures are identifiable without digging through
a single combined log. Also adds a `format:check` task that runs
swiftformat in lint-only mode, since `format` still writes changes in
place locally.

Bump CI action versions

Update actions/checkout to v6 and jdx/mise-action to v4 across both
workflows.

Separate raw scripts from spinner-decorated mise tasks

Scripts (format.sh, format-check.sh, lint.sh, test.sh, build.sh,
install.sh, run.sh, setup.sh) are now plain bash with pass-through
logs — no spinner, no _lib.sh sourcing inside the script itself. Dev
mise tasks wrap each script with run_step so local output still gets
the spinner treatment; CI uses a parallel set of ci:* tasks that
invoke the scripts directly so GitHub Actions logs show full output.
The combined check.sh/check-fix.sh wrappers are replaced by mise
task `depends` composition.

Quiet mise task output and serialize check composites

Set `task.output = "quiet"` so mise stops printing the `$ cmd` echo
line for every subtask — the run_step spinner already conveys which
step is running. Also switch `check` / `check:fix` from `depends` to
`run = [{ tasks = ... }]` so the subtasks execute sequentially in a
predictable order instead of parallel.

Split Checks workflow into Format, Lint, and Test workflows

Each check now runs as its own workflow so they appear as three
independent status checks on pull requests and can be re-run
individually. Format and Lint skip the GhosttyKit download since they
don't need to build the Swift target; Test still fetches it.

Combine Format/Lint/Test into one workflow with parallel jobs

Three separate workflow files meant three separate PR status entries
but also three separate workflow runs in the Actions UI. Consolidate
into one `Checks` workflow with three parallel jobs — same parallelism
(jobs run concurrently unless linked by `needs`), cleaner Actions tab,
and a single status summary per run.

Migrate test suite from XCTest to Swift Testing

Use @Test/@Suite/#expect/#require instead of XCTestCase, which matches
the framework Swift Package Manager actually discovers (the legacy
XCTest tests were silently producing 0 results).

Pass scripts as run_step commands so dev task output is silenced

Previously the spinner printed, then the script ran raw with full
output visible — defeating the purpose of run_step. Now each script
runs under run_step, which hides logs on success and prints them on
failure.

Add Sparkle-based auto-updates

Bake an EdDSA public key into Info.plist so updates verify against our
private key without needing an Apple Developer ID. Sparkle downloads
through its own networking path, so installed updates launch without
the com.apple.quarantine attribute — users only do the right-click Open
dance once on initial install. Release workflow signs each DMG with
sign_update and appends an item to the appcast served from gh-pages.
Rename Sparkle secrets to a consistent SPARKLE_ED_* prefix

Extract appcast publishing into a script

The inline YAML heredoc broke block-scalar indentation rules; moving
it into scripts/publish-appcast.sh keeps the workflow file valid and
makes the logic easier to iterate on locally.
Bump artifact actions to latest majors (upload v7, download v6)

Document current Gatekeeper first-launch flow

macOS Sequoia/Tahoe no longer allows right-click → Open to bypass
Gatekeeper for unsigned apps; users must use the Open Anyway button in
System Settings → Privacy & Security. Keep the xattr fallback for
Terminal-savvy users.

Ship a single universal DMG per release

Sparkle picks the first <item> in the appcast as the update candidate;
when we shipped separate arm64 and x86_64 DMGs Sparkle tested the wrong
enclosure against the host and silently reported "up to date" instead of
looking further. Merge both slices with lipo into one binary, drop the
CI matrix, and publish a single Macterm-<version>.dmg per release.

Use release version for CFBundleVersion so Sparkle sees newer builds

Sparkle compares the appcast's sparkle:version against the installed
app's CFBundleVersion, not CFBundleShortVersionString. Our old build
number was a git rev-list count, which stayed identical when two tags
pointed at the same commit — Sparkle concluded 'up to date' even though
a newer tag was available. Match CFBundleVersion to the release string
so each tag produces a strictly greater comparable value.

fix: bundle ghostty terminfo so TERM=xterm-ghostty resolves standalone

Since 1.13.3, Macterm points GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR at its own bundle to run
without a Ghostty.app install, but the bundle shipped only themes +
shell-integration — no terminfo. That left TERM=xterm-ghostty unresolvable for

<bundle>/terminfo — libghostty's own dirname(GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR)/terminfo
derivation would point outside Resources given Macterm's bundle layout.

Factor the resource/terminfo selection into a pure GhosttyResourceResolver and
add tests: GhosttyResourceResolverTests covers the selection logic, and

can't recur silently.

fix: always resolve resources from our own bundle, ignoring inherited env

matched a known path (e.g. an installed Ghostty.app or Macterm.app), skipping
the TERMINFO handling entirely. A stale value pointing at an install without
terminfo then let libghostty derive a broken TERMINFO (Contents/terminfo),
reintroducing the #39/#40 garbled-key symptom even with a fixed bundle.

Drop the early return so the bundle-first resolver always runs: our own
complete bundle wins, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR + TERMINFO are set explicitly, and
external dirs only serve as fallback when the bundle lacks resources.

fix: ship resources in Ghostty.app layout so libghostty derives TERMINFO right

The earlier attempt shipped terminfo flat in Contents/Resources/ and set
TERMINFO explicitly. That can't work: libghostty overwrites TERMINFO at shell
spawn with dirname(GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR)/terminfo (src/termio/Exec.zig), so the
setenv was clobbered and TERM=xterm-ghostty stayed broken (verified: the spawned
shell saw TERMINFO=.../Contents/terminfo, a nonexistent path).

Mirror a real Ghostty.app instead: ship resources under Resources/ghostty/
(themes + shell-integration) with the compiled terminfo DB at the sibling
Resources/terminfo/, and point GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR at Resources/ghostty. Now
libghostty's own derivation lands on Resources/terminfo, which resolves
xterm-ghostty. Drop the useless explicit TERMINFO setenv.

BundledResourcesTests now asserts the load-bearing invariant: terminfo is a
sibling of ghostty/, never inside it.

fix: respect light/dark theme split in app chrome (#38)

Macterm rendered the light side of a `theme = light:X,dark:Y` Ghostty config
for its own chrome (window, sidebar, palette) regardless of the system
appearance, and never switched on a light/dark toggle.

libghostty applies the active color scheme only to the terminal *surface* at
render time; the config object's color getters always resolve a split to the
`light:` side and the raw `theme` value isn't readable back through the C API.
So the chrome — which derives from those getters — couldn't see the dark side.

ThemeResolver now parses the user's effective `theme`, picks the side matching
NSApp.effectiveAppearance, and reads that theme file's colors directly;
GhosttyApp's color accessors prefer those for a split (and fall back to the
config getters for a plain theme). A KVO observer on effectiveAppearance bumps
the observable configVersion and posts .mactermConfigDidChange on every system
switch, and an AppColorScheme modifier reads configVersion so SwiftUI
re-evaluates preferredColorScheme and all MactermTheme colors — without it the
chrome froze at its launch appearance. The observer is registered off the init
stack to avoid re-entering GhosttyApp.shared's dispatch_once.

feat: native overlay scrollbar for terminal panes

Terminal panes had no scrollbar — you could scroll the scrollback with
the trackpad but had no visual indication of position and no draggable
scroller. This adds a native macOS overlay scrollbar following Ghostty's
1.3.0+ approach: nest the Metal surface inside a standard NSScrollView
whose blank documentView is sized to the full scrollback height, so
AppKit renders and hit-tests a real overlay scroller (auto-hide/fade for
free) while the surface only draws the visible viewport.

Scrollback geometry flows in via the GHOSTTY_ACTION_SCROLLBAR action;
scroller drags flow out via the scroll_to_row keybind action. Wheel
events are untouched — the surface still forwards them to libghostty,
which decides scrollback vs cursor-keys vs mouse-report, so alt-screen
apps keep working.

The scroll view is owned by Pane (like the surface NSView) so it
survives tab switches and split reshapes and sidesteps the persistence
bug ghostty-org/ghostty#9444.

Stop the tag stamp from laundering a stale GhosttyKit as pinned (#222)

setup.sh wrote .ghosttykit-tag whenever the artifact dirs merely existed, without checking that this run downloaded anything. A checkout predating the pin — or one where only zmx was missing — got the current pin stamped over artifacts from some other release, and every later run then saw a stamp agreeing with GHOSTTYKIT_TAG and never refreshed. Staleness became invisible and permanent.

A real checkout was found in that state, stamped build-2026-08-02: terminfo three weeks older than the tag, beside a framework whose ghostty.h was 36357 bytes against the release's 36582 — two artifacts from two different releases, with 24 renumbered ghostty_action_tag_e constants.

Gate the write on the need_* flags, so the stamp only ever describes what the run actually installed. A pin bump sets both, so the case the stamp exists for still records itself. An absent stamp now means "provenance unknown" rather than "matches the pin", and warn_unstamped_artifacts says so with rm -rf remediation instead of either lying or forcing a re-download. CI is exempt by construction: .ghosttykit-tag joins the cached paths, so a restored tree arrives stamped.

Pin GhosttyKit to build-2026-09-20, for a resize that moves by pixels

A grid only comes in whole rows, so the leftover height of a pane grows
as it is resized until it is a full row and the viewport takes one — and
at that instant everything on screen jumps a cell, because the row it
gains is pulled in from scrollback at the top. Dragging a split divider
slowly, the text sat still, jumped, sat still; every split animation did
the same, a dozen times in 300ms. No reflow is involved, so a stacked
split with no width change showed it just as plainly.

The fix is in the fork (thdxg/ghostty#9): under `smooth-scroll` the
renderer hands the render state the height its rows don't account for,
which adds to whatever remainder a scroll gesture left, and the grid is
drawn that much lower with the row above partly revealed. The content
then slides as the leftover grows and the row it gains arrives where
the revealed sliver had got to.

The API review is empty — zero changed header lines across the 170
symbols Macterm references, so this carries four days of upstream with
no surface of ours moving.
